questions.stem: When are the offices in a hotel or villa usually cleaned?
options: In the middle of the working day, while staff are busy
Before or after office hours, as the schedule says
Only when the manager complains that it is dirty
Once a month, on the day the bills are paid

questions.stem: You must clean the accounts office, which is kept locked. How should you get in?
options: Borrow a key from a co-worker who has one
Ask the security guard to open it with any key that fits
Climb in through the window if it is open
Sign out the key as the property's rules say

questions.stem: What should you check before starting to clean a manager's office?
options: That no one is working there, or that they agree to it
That the manager's desk drawers are open for dusting
That the computer is switched on so you can check it
That the phone is off the hook so it will not ring

questions.stem: Which equipment would you usually take to clean an office?
options: A floor stripping machine and a pressure washer
An ironer and some fabric softener
Dusters, cloths, a vacuum and bin liners
A ladder, a paint roller and a tin of white paint

questions.stem: A computer cable runs across the office floor where people walk. What should you do?
options: Unplug it and roll it up neatly in the corner
Pull it tight so it lies flat on the carpet
Report it so it can be moved or covered safely
Tape it down yourself with sticky parcel tape

questions.stem: Why should you never spray cleaner straight onto a computer keyboard or phone?
options: Liquid can get inside and damage it or cause a shock
The spray will make the keys too slippery to type on
The cleaner will make the phone ring by itself
The keyboard letters will turn a different colour

questions.stem: An office worker has left a computer switched on. What should you do?
options: Switch it off at the wall so it saves electricity
Use it to check your own e-mail while you clean
Unplug it so you can dust behind the desk
Leave it on, and do not touch the keys or screen

questions.stem: A box of copier paper is heavy. How should you move it to the store cupboard?
options: Lift it from the floor with your legs kept straight
Use a trolley, or lift it close with bent knees
Kick it along the floor to the cupboard
Throw it up onto the top shelf in one go

questions.stem: How should you clean a computer screen, unless the maker's instructions say otherwise?
options: With a soft, dry or slightly damp cloth, or a screen wipe
With a scouring pad dipped in a little bleach
With glass cleaner sprayed straight on the screen
With a wet cloth from the mop bucket, then left to dry

questions.stem: A desk is covered with papers. How should you clean it?
options: Stack all the papers in one neat pile and wipe the desk
Put the papers in the drawer, then polish the whole top
Leave the papers as they are and dust the clear parts
Throw away loose papers and clean the whole surface

questions.stem: Why are telephone handsets and keyboards wiped with a disinfectant wipe or cloth?
options: To make them shine for photographs of the office
To stop the phone from ringing during the night
To remove fingerprints so no one knows who used them
They are touched a lot and can spread germs

questions.stem: Which product is usually best for wiping a laminated office desk?
options: Neat bleach poured from the bottle
A neutral cleaner on a damp cloth
Scouring powder and a hard scrub brush
Furniture wax rubbed in very thickly

questions.stem: While emptying a bin, you see a letter about a staff member's pay. What should you do?
options: Read it, as it was thrown away and is no longer private
Tell your co-workers what it says at lunch
Do not read it; deal with it as confidential waste
Take it home to use the back as scrap paper

questions.stem: Some offices have a locked bin or bag for confidential waste. What is it for?
options: Papers that must be shredded so no one can read them
Food waste from the office kitchen and the fridge
Empty bottles, cans and plastic for recycling
Broken glass and used batteries from the office

questions.stem: The office phone rings while you are cleaning. What should you usually do?
options: Answer it and give the caller any information they ask for
Let it ring, or take a message only if that is the rule
Unplug the phone so that it stops ringing for the night
Answer it and say the manager has left the company

questions.stem: Why must office cleaners keep what they see in offices private?
options: So the cleaners can sell the information later
Because cleaners are not allowed to talk at all
So the office staff do not have to lock anything
Offices hold private details of guests and staff

questions.stem: Which item belongs in the office paper recycling bin?
options: A used coffee cup with some milk still in it
A broken light bulb wrapped in paper
Clean scrap paper that is not confidential
A greasy paper plate from lunch

questions.stem: How should you deal with an office shredder bin that is full?
options: Switch it off and unplug it before emptying the bin
Push the paper down by hand while it is running
Leave it running and pull the bin out quickly
Pour water in so that the paper takes less room

options: Burn them with the garden waste behind the villa
Put them in the paper recycling bin with the paper
Pour the ink down the office sink and bin the rest
Put them aside for the special waste or recycling

options: Leave the parts under the desks, as no one sees them
Pull out chairs, vacuum under, then put them back
Push the desks against the wall with the computers on
Lift each chair onto a desk and leave it there

questions.stem: An office chair mat (the plastic sheet under a desk chair) is dusty. How should it be cleaned?
options: Wipe it with a damp cloth and neutral cleaner, then dry
Scrub it with scouring powder until it goes cloudy
Leave it outside in the hot sun so that the dust blows off it
Polish it with floor wax so the chair rolls faster

options: Full of old food, so staff can share what is left
Switched off at night to save power, with food inside
Clean, with old food removed as the rules say
Warm, with the door open so it does not smell

options: To stop them using power while you clean the floor
To avoid an electric shock while you wipe them
So the cleaning chemical can soak into the plug
So that the kettle cools faster with the door open

questions.stem: At what temperature should an office fridge keep food? (Or as the Centre's food safety plan says.)
options: 15 °C or below
10 °C or below
8 °C or below
5 °C or below

questions.stem: Part of preparing an office is restocking supplies. Which of these would you usually check?
options: Paper towels, hand soap, drinking water and cups
The manager's cash box and the petty cash float in it
The staff's private lockers and handbags
The guests' passports kept in the office safe

questions.stem: The office printer shows "paper low". If refilling it is part of your job, what should you do?
options: Push in as much paper as will fit, even if it bends
Use paper from the confidential waste bin
Load paper as the printer's guide shows
Switch off the printer and leave a note for staff

questions.stem: You are asked to set up a meeting room for ten people sitting round one long table. Which layout is this?
options: Theatre style
Classroom style
Cabaret style
Boardroom style

questions.stem: Which meeting room layout has rows of chairs only, all facing the front, with no tables?
options: Boardroom style
Theatre style

options: That the curtains are closed and the lights are off
That the chairs are stacked so the room looks bigger

questions.stem: Which items are usually set at each place for a business meeting?
options: A notepad, a pen, and a glass for water
A pillow, a blanket and a reading lamp
A bath towel, soap and a face cloth
A cutting board, a knife and a fork

options: By putting your fingers inside the rim to carry more
By the base or lower part, never touching the rim
By the top edge, so you do not drop them

options: Leave it as it is until the next meeting is booked
Lock it at once, with all the used cups still left inside
Take home the pens and notepads that were left
Clear it, hand in left items, and reset it as asked

questions.stem: When you have finished cleaning an office, what should you do before leaving?
options: Check windows are shut and lock the door as the rules say
Leave the door open so the air can dry the floor
Leave the lights on so the office looks busy
Hide the key under the door mat for the next shift

questions.stem: A person you do not know asks you to let them into the general manager's office to collect a file. What should you do?
options: Let them in, as long as they are quick about it
Let them in and stay with them while they look
Politely say no, and call security or a manager
Give them your key so they can lock up afterwards

questions.stem: Why must you sign for office keys when you take them and when you return them?
options: So that you are paid for the hours you worked
So the key can be copied for each of the cleaners
So the manager knows when to change the locks
So it is known who has each key at any time

questions.stem: How should indoor plants in an office be cared for, if this is part of your job?
options: Water them every hour so the soil is always wet
Water them as the care plan says and wipe dusty leaves
Spray them with furniture polish to make the leaves shine
Move them into the dark store room overnight

questions.stem: How should you clean a glass partition or door in an office?
options: Spray glass cleaner onto a cloth and wipe from the top down
Wipe it with the cloth used on the bin lids
Splash plenty of water on it and let it dry by itself in the air
Rub it with a dry paper towel and furniture polish

questions.stem: While cleaning an office, you find the air conditioning is leaking water onto a desk. What should you do?
options: Move the papers to the floor and leave a bucket
Switch off the main power supply for the whole building
Protect the desk if safe, and report it straight away
Wipe it up and say nothing, as it will soon stop

questions.stem: You notice the office window lock is broken. Who should you tell?
options: The first guest you happen to see in the lobby
Your supervisor or maintenance, straight away
No one, as windows are not part of your job
A friend, so they can fix it on the weekend

questions.stem: What is the best way to clean office door handles and light switches?
options: With a dry duster only, to save cleaning products
With the toilet cloth, as it is already wet
With a wet sponge squeezed onto the switch
With a cloth damp with disinfectant, not dripping

questions.stem: Why is a checklist used when cleaning and preparing offices?
options: So that the cleaner can work without any supervisor
So the office staff can mark the cleaner out of ten
So no task is missed and the work can be checked
So the cleaner has something to read on the break

questions.stem: Where should you keep the cleaning chemicals while you clean an office?
options: In your caddy, with you, closed and labelled
On the office desk next to the staff's cups
In the office fridge so that they stay nice and cool
On the floor in the doorway for easy reach

questions.stem: A staff member has left a cup of coffee and a plate on the desk. What is usually expected?
options: Drink the coffee yourself so that it is not wasted
Leave them for a week to teach the staff a lesson
Put them in the desk drawer, out of sight of guests
Clear them to the kitchen, as the rules say

questions.stem: Why should office chairs be pushed in neatly when you finish?
options: So the vacuum cleaner can be left under the desk
The office looks tidy and walkways are kept clear
So staff cannot sit down until the manager arrives
So the chairs do not get any dust on them

questions.stem: At the end of your office cleaning round, what should you do with your record sheet?
options: Throw it away, as the offices are now clean
Keep it at home in case you need it one day
Fill it in, note any faults, and hand it in

essays.stem: Describe how to clean and prepare a manager's office in a hotel, from getting in to locking up.
essays.modelAnswer: I sign out the key from the key log as the rules say and collect my caddy, cloths, vacuum, bin liners and supplies. I knock before entering, even out of hours, and if someone is working I ask when it suits them. I switch on the lights and open the blinds. I empty the bins, keeping general waste, recycling and confidential waste apart, and I do not read any papers. I dust from high to low, then damp wipe the desk, working round papers and personal items without moving or reading them. I clean the phone and keyboard with a disinfectant wipe or a cloth, never spraying liquid onto them, and I wipe the screen with a soft cloth. I clean door handles, light switches and glass. I vacuum the carpet, pulling chairs out and pushing them back in. I restock water, cups and paper towels as needed. Last I check the room, shut the windows, switch off the lights, lock the door, sign the key back in and note any faults on my checklist.
markingPoints: Signs out the key and prepares equipment and supplies
Knocks first and respects anyone working
Empties bins correctly, keeping confidential waste apart and not reading papers
Dusts and wipes round papers; cleans phones, keyboards and screens without spraying them
Vacuums, restocks, secures the room, returns the key and records faults

essays.stem: Explain how to clean office equipment such as computers, keyboards, phones and printers safely.
essays.modelAnswer: Office equipment is electrical and often holds important work, so I take care. I never switch off, unplug or use a computer without permission, and I do not press keys or move the mouse. I never spray liquid straight onto any equipment, because it can get inside, damage it or cause a shock. Instead I put a little cleaner, or the product the maker suggests, onto a soft cloth and wring it out well. For screens I use a soft dry or slightly damp microfibre cloth or a screen wipe, wiping gently, never with glass cleaner or scouring products. I wipe keyboards, mice and phone handsets with a disinfectant wipe or a damp cloth, because many hands touch them and germs spread. I dust the outsides of printers and photocopiers but do not open them or touch the paper path or toner. I keep cables where they are and report any that are damaged or trailing across a walkway. If anything is wet, sparking or smells hot, I keep away and report it at once.
markingPoints: Does not switch off, unplug or use equipment without permission
Never sprays liquid onto equipment; puts a little on a cloth
Screens: soft or microfibre cloth or screen wipe, gently
Disinfects keyboards, mice and phones because of germs
Leaves cables and printer insides alone; reports damage or faults

essays.stem: Explain why confidentiality matters when cleaning offices, and how a cleaner protects it.
essays.modelAnswer: Offices in a hotel or villa hold private information about guests and staff, such as names, passport details, credit card slips, pay, bookings and business plans. If this is seen or shared, guests and staff can be harmed, the business can lose trust and money, and the law on personal information may be broken. A cleaner protects it in several ways. I do not read papers, screens, letters or notes on desks, and I do not move them; I clean round them. I do not use computers or phones. I put papers from confidential bins or bags only where the property says, ready for shredding, and never in the general rubbish or recycling, and I never take scrap paper home. I do not answer the office phone unless that is my job, and I never give out guest or staff details. I keep office doors and filing cabinets locked as I found them. I do not talk about what I have seen, even to co-workers or friends.
markingPoints: Names private information held in offices
Explains the harm if it is shared
Does not read, move or use papers, screens or computers
Handles confidential waste correctly, never in general waste or taken home
Does not give out details or gossip; keeps doors and cabinets locked

essays.stem: Describe how you would set up a meeting room for a 12-person boardroom meeting at a hotel.
essays.modelAnswer: First I read the booking sheet for the time, the number of people, the layout, the equipment and any refreshments or special requests. I clean the room: I dust, wipe the table and chairs, clean glass and touch points, and vacuum. I set out the table in boardroom style, with 12 chairs evenly spaced, five on each long side and one at each end, or as the sheet says. I check the lights, the AC and the blinds. I set up and test the equipment, such as the projector, screen, speaker phone, extension leads and the Wi-Fi details, and I tape down or tidy any cables so no one trips. At each place I put a notepad, a pen and the agenda if given, and a clean glass, held by the base. I put jugs or bottles of water on the table, with coasters. I put a sign on the door if the property uses one. I check the room as a guest would and tell my supervisor or the organiser that it is ready.
markingPoints: Reads the booking sheet for numbers, layout, equipment and requests
Cleans the room before setting up
Sets the boardroom layout with the correct number of evenly spaced chairs
Tests equipment and makes cables safe
Sets notepads, pens, agendas, glasses held by the base, and water; checks and reports it ready

essays.stem: Explain how you would deal with the different kinds of waste found in offices.
essays.modelAnswer: Offices produce several kinds of waste, and each must go to the right place. General waste, such as food wrappers, tissues and sweepings, goes into the normal bin bag. I tie the bag, lift it by the neck and hold it away from my body in case of sharp items, and I never push waste down with my hand. Clean paper, card, plastic bottles and cans go into the recycling bins, as the property's system says, without food or liquid in them. Confidential waste, such as old guest forms, receipts and staff papers, goes into the locked bin or bag for shredding, and I never read it or put it with recycling. If I empty a shredder, I switch it off and unplug it first. Special waste, such as printer cartridges, batteries, broken light bulbs and old electrical items, is kept apart and handed in for safe disposal or recycling. Food waste from the kitchenette is bagged and taken out often, because in Jamaica's heat it soon smells and draws ants and flies.
markingPoints: General waste bagged and handled safely by the neck
Recycling kept clean and sorted as the property's system says
Confidential waste kept for shredding, never read or recycled
Shredder switched off and unplugged before emptying; special waste kept apart
Food waste removed often because of heat and pests

essays.stem: Explain how to clean the staff kitchenette in an office block and keep it hygienic.
essays.modelAnswer: I wear gloves and use a food-safe cleaner, measured as the label says. I keep my kitchen cloths separate from the toilet cloths, as the colour code says. I wash any cups and plates left out, or put them in the dishwasher, and put them away. I unplug the kettle, microwave and coffee maker before I clean them. I wipe inside the microwave, the kettle outside and the coffee maker drip tray, and I descale the kettle when needed, as the maker says. I clean the sink and taps and wipe the worktops, then disinfect them. I clean the fridge handle and check the fridge is cold, at 5 °C or below or as the property's food safety plan says. On the set day I remove old or out-of-date food as the property's rules say, and wipe the shelves. I empty the bin often, because food waste in the heat draws ants and flies. I restock cups, tea, coffee, sugar, paper towels and soap. Last I mop the floor and put out a wet floor sign.
markingPoints: Gloves, food-safe cleaner and separate kitchen cloths
Washes and puts away crockery
Unplugs appliances before cleaning them; cleans kettle, microwave and coffee maker
Cleans and disinfects sink and worktops; checks the fridge temperature and removes old food as the rules say
Empties bins often, restocks and mops with a wet floor sign

essays.stem: Explain the security steps a cleaner should follow when cleaning offices out of hours.
essays.modelAnswer: Out of hours there are fewer people about, so offices are at more risk. I sign the keys out and back in on the key log, and I keep them on me all the time; I never lend them or leave them in a door. If there is an alarm, I follow the property's procedure for it. I unlock only the office I am cleaning and lock it again when I leave it, even for a short time. I never let anyone into an office, even if they say they work there; I politely say no and call security or the duty manager. I do not prop open fire doors or back doors to carry out rubbish. I do not touch safes, cash boxes, filing cabinets or computers. When I finish I check that windows are shut and locked, lights and equipment are off as the rules say, and the door is locked. I report anything unusual, such as an open door, a broken lock, a stranger or a missing item, to security or my supervisor straight away.
markingPoints: Signs keys in and out and keeps them on the person
Follows the alarm procedure and locks each office when leaving it
Never lets anyone in; calls security or the duty manager
Does not prop doors or touch safes, cash or files
Checks windows and doors at the end and reports anything unusual

essays.stem: Explain the main hazards for a cleaner in offices, and how to deal with each one.
essays.modelAnswer: Electrical equipment is a hazard. I do not spray liquid on computers, phones or sockets, I unplug small items such as kettles before cleaning them, and I report damaged plugs, cables or sockets. Trailing cables and extension leads can trip people, so I do not stretch my vacuum cable across walkways, and I report loose cables instead of moving them myself. Overloaded power strips can overheat, so I report them. Lifting boxes of paper or bins can hurt my back, so I bend my knees, keep the load close, use a trolley and get help with heavy items. Cleaning chemicals can harm skin, eyes and lungs, so I read the label and SDS, wear gloves, measure dilutions and never mix products. A shredder can catch fingers, hair, ties or jewellery, so I switch it off and unplug it before emptying it. Wet floors in the kitchenette are slippery, so I use a wet floor sign. Sharp items such as staples and broken glass may be in bins, so I handle bags carefully.
markingPoints: Electrical equipment: no liquid sprays, unplug, report damage
Trailing cables and overloaded sockets: keep walkways clear and report
Manual handling: bend knees, trolley, help
Chemicals: label and SDS, gloves, dilution, no mixing
Shredder, wet floors and sharps in bins handled safely

essays.stem: Explain how you would clear and reset a meeting room after a meeting, including any items left behind.
essays.modelAnswer: I wait until the meeting has finished and the guests have left, or the organiser says I may start. I knock and check the room is empty. I look for items left behind, such as phones, laptops, chargers, glasses or folders. I do not open or read them. I hand them to my supervisor or the front desk so they can be logged as lost property and returned. Papers and notes left on the table may be confidential, so I put them aside for the organiser or in the confidential waste bin, as the property's rules say, and never in the general bin. I clear used glasses, cups and water jugs to the kitchen. I empty the bins. I switch off the projector and equipment as the instructions say, let the projector cool if it needs to, and tidy the cables. I wipe the table, chairs and touch points and vacuum the floor. Then I reset the room to the next layout on the booking sheet, or to its standard set-up, and report any damage or faulty equipment.
markingPoints: Starts only when the meeting is over and the room is empty
Hands in left items to be logged without opening them
Treats left papers as confidential
Clears glasses and bins, switches off equipment correctly and cleans the room
Resets to the next layout and reports damage or faults

essays.stem: Explain how you would plan the cleaning of several offices in a villa company's head office during one shift.
essays.modelAnswer: At the start of the shift I check the cleaning schedule and checklist to see which offices to clean, which tasks are daily and which are weekly, and any notes, such as a meeting room needed at 8 a.m. I put first the rooms that are needed soonest, such as a meeting room or the reception office, and leave offices where people are still working until they have left. I collect and check my equipment and supplies so I do not waste time going back to the store. I sign out the keys I need. I plan a route that moves through the building in order, so I do not walk back and forth, and I do the same jobs in the same order in each office, such as bins, dusting, desks, equipment, touch points and floors last. I keep to the time each task should take, but I do not skip safety steps. I tick off each task on the checklist as I finish it, note faults or problems, and tell my supervisor if I cannot finish something.
markingPoints: Uses the schedule and checklist, including daily and weekly tasks
Puts rooms needed soonest first and fits round staff still working
Prepares equipment and keys in advance
Plans a sensible route and the same task order in each office
Ticks off the checklist, records faults and tells the supervisor of anything not done

practical1.title: Clean and prepare an office ready for the working day
practical1.brief: As a group, clean and prepare the Centre's office (or a training room set up as a villa company office, with two desks, a computer, a phone, a printer, papers, a staff kitchenette corner and bins for general waste, recycling and confidential waste). The assessor acts as the office manager and has left some items to test you, such as papers on a desk, a computer left on, a used cup, a trailing cable and an item of special waste. Work in these stages: (1) sign out the key, read the checklist and share out the tasks; (2) enter correctly, open blinds and empty the bins, keeping each kind of waste apart; (3) dust from high to low and damp wipe the desks, working round papers; (4) clean the phone, keyboard and screen safely; (5) clean the kitchenette corner, with appliances unplugged; (6) disinfect door handles and light switches and clean the glass; (7) vacuum, with chairs pulled out and pushed back; (8) restock supplies, check the room, report faults, lock up and sign the key back in. Every member leads at least one stage and cleans at least one piece of equipment while the assessor watches. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Cleaning caddy with dusters, microfibre cloths and colour-coded cloths
Neutral cleaner, disinfectant wipes or solution and glass cleaner, with labels and SDS
Screen wipes or a soft cloth for screens
Bin liners, a recycling bag and a confidential waste bag
Supplies to restock: paper towels, cups, water and stationery
Key log, office checklist and a fault report form
A phone or camera for the photos
photos: The key signed out and the group's task list
The bins emptied, with general, recycling, confidential and special waste kept apart
A desk wiped with the papers left in place
The phone, keyboard and screen being cleaned with the cloth, not sprayed
The kitchenette corner cleaned, with appliances unplugged
The vacuumed floor with chairs pushed in
The completed checklist, fault report and key signed back in
checklist: Signed the key out and back in correctly
Kept general, recycling, confidential and special waste apart and did not read papers
Cleaned round papers and personal items without moving them
Cleaned electrical equipment safely, never spraying it, and left the computer as found
Unplugged kitchenette appliances before cleaning them
Disinfected touch points and left glass free of smears
Vacuumed fully under desks and left the office tidy
Reported the trailing cable and any faults on the form
Locked up correctly and took a full part in the group
safety: Never spray liquid onto computers, phones, printers or sockets
Unplug the kettle and microwave before cleaning them
Do not move or unplug cables you did not plug in; report trailing cables
Read labels, wear gloves and never mix products; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
Lift boxes and bins with bent knees, or use a trolley

practical2.title: Set up a meeting room for 12 people and reset it afterwards
practical2.brief: As a group, prepare a training room at the Centre as a hotel meeting room, from a booking sheet the assessor gives you (for example, a 12-person boardroom meeting for a tour company, 9 a.m., with a projector and water). Work in these stages: (1) read the booking sheet and plan who does what; (2) clean the room: dust, wipe the table and chairs, clean the glass and touch points, and vacuum; (3) set the tables and 12 chairs in boardroom style, evenly spaced; (4) set up and test the projector and screen, and make the cables safe; (5) set each place with a notepad, pen, agenda and clean glass, and put out water and coasters; (6) check the room and tell the assessor it is ready; (7) the assessor then holds a short mock meeting and leaves used glasses, notes and a phone behind; (8) clear the room, hand in the phone to be logged, deal with the notes as confidential, and reset the room to theatre style for the next booking. Every member sets at least three places and takes part in both the set-up and the reset, and one member explains the set-up to the assessor. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A booking sheet from the assessor
Projector, screen and an extension lead
Notepads, pens and copies of an agenda
Clean glasses, water jugs or bottles, and coasters
Cleaning caddy, cloths and a vacuum cleaner
A phone or camera for the photos
photos: The booking sheet and the group's plan
